gaps.claim: memories.py crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on a cp1250 console when a memory body carries U+2192; it is the last command of the pass's own step 0. Four scripts had each pasted the same three-line fix into their own main().

`^\s*applies:\s*(.+)$` matches the newline in multiline mode, so a YAML block list (which the memory harness rewrites inline lists into) reads as its first item. Two memories applied to a class named '- correspondence' and would never have been printed for anything.

An unreadable run record parses as {} and is then deleted: not young (started_at ''), no results so neither scope nor last-fired, and if untracked and uncited it is a victim. Rule 8 broken in the only script that deletes.

An accepted order whose position_id is absent from their positions endpoint is silently skipped, so its capital never counts as deployed and affordable() authorises spending it again. The comment says 'worth noticing' and nothing notices.

A thread reconstructed from their side alone gets asked_at_from None when no receipt timestamp is readable, and the row builder turns None into 'us' -- a proxy labelled as our own record, in the rows that feed the Stats tab.

An MCP tool the registry does not classify falls off the end of the MUTATE branch and is permitted with full arguments. SAFE raises and PROBE forces empty args; MUTATE, the only tier that can spend, is default-allow.
The delete loop has no per-file error handling: one PermissionError (a record held open by a concurrent pytest on Windows) kills it after some files are gone and before anything is printed.
verified_by_us sums REPRODUCING->PASSING transitions rather than distinct findings, so a bug that regressed and was fixed again counts twice in the figure the operator asked for.
A 200 whose body is not shaped {positions:[...]} reads as an empty holding and frees the whole bankroll. buy() in the same file unwraps payload['result']; this does not.
min((str(r.get('at') or '') for r in receipts), default='') returns '' whenever any receipt lacks a timestamp, discarding a readable one from another receipt on the same thread.
assert paper is True is documented as the barrier somebody must delete on purpose; python -O strips it. The docstring claims a protection this line does not give.

The deep pass's step 1b retires a memory by dropping its line from MEMORY.md and leaving the file. That guard then reports 'not linked from MEMORY.md, so no session knows it exists' -- so a retirement performed exactly as the skill prescribes turns tests/repo red, which step 6 runs and step 9 reverts a night over. The guard cannot tell a deliberate retirement from a forgotten file, and the skill's own procedure is the input that breaks it. Found by performing the procedure.

Greps the TEXT of scripts/submit.py for the literal 'public repo: github.com/zakutana' and for 'evidence retained'; the module is exec'd and never called, no payload composed. Rebuilding the line as "(public repo: " + REPO_URL + ")" restores the private link with the check green; 'evidence retained' surviving only in a comment also passes. The sibling check for verify.py does it correctly -- it calls body() and greps the composed evidence.

The paragraph must describe the fingerprint IN THE SAME PAYLOAD. The check only asserts body() prints the sentence matching the `identity` the TEST hands it. verify.py sends row['check']['pinned_fingerprint'] but derives identity from the CURRENT run's measurement.fingerprint, so a row pinned to an AST-era value whose check now declares one gets the claims.yaml sentence beside an AST hash -- the named defect, recreated. identity_kind has no test anywhere.

Contract: 'their figure, and ours must agree with it or say why.' Their figure sits in the same fixture (leaderboard total_paid) and is never compared; only reward_currency is read from it. _rewards() counts len(rows) and ignores our_reports.total (44) and total_paid (37000), so a windowed my-reports read prints 20000 beside their 37000 with nothing failing.

Contract: ONE read switch, bell and chip calling the same markRead 'or the two would drift'. Asserts template.count('markRead()') >= 2, which is 3 today only because the function DEFINITION contains the substring. A separate markChangedRead() with its own watermark still counts 2. Sorting oldest-first also leaves the marker untouched.

The docstring's whole claim is that this EXECUTES the sort and the chips. The harness stubs querySelectorAll() to [], so the comparator and changedSince(el.dataset.changedAt) never run over a single row. A typo in dataset.changedAt or in the row's data-changed-at attribute makes every row read as unchanged, exit 0, green.

Contract: 'a row added to CLAUDE.md appears ON THE PAGE.' Both sides are Python parsers; neither touches TEMPLATE. Deleting the only site that reads D.help.models leaves both parsers agreeing and the page showing nothing.

(a) the fixture's only self-test carries component=meta.pipeline, dropped at section=='_meta' BEFORE the SELF_TEST_DIRS filter, so removing that filter entirely keeps the assertion green. (b) the questions.get() substitution for parametrised reconciliation cases is asserted nowhere -- the live loop only checks doc is non-empty, so the wrong check's first line would pass.

Docstring promises 'a journalled intent still wins where one exists, so nothing about a2a.py's contract changes'. The fixture has no intent, so inverting the precedence is invisible here; the sibling with an intent cannot see it either (both timestamps round to 90 minutes and it never asserts asked_at_from == 'us').

(a) FALSE PASS: positions_grew is (after['positions'] or 0) - (before['positions'] or 0), and _snapshot writes 'positions' only on a 200 -- a failed read gives 0-39 = -39, the trade drops out of `landed`, subject is empty and the verdict is 'passed' with the reason 'each buy debited the balance by its own notional' while nothing moved. Rule 8 inverted, on the row that would flip #87 to VERIFIED FIXED. (b) FALSE FAIL: silent is abs(moved-usdc)>0.01, so a 1.00 buy debited 0.97 files 'moved the paper balance by nothing' while quoting 'the balance moved 0.97'. The docstring's contract is 'costs something'; the assertion demands exactly-the-notional.

waited_seconds is not time since the question was asked: _poll sets started = time.monotonic() on entry and `nexus.py answer` calls _poll again, so the clock restarts on every pick-up. The recorded data proves it -- NEX-0001 asked 10:03:06, gave_up 10:28:33, waited_seconds 0.0. Ask at 10:00, give up at 10:15, re-poll at 11:00: an answer row lands with waited_seconds ~0 and five such rows slide the gave_up rows out of WINDOW=5, so the check reads 'all 5 answered inside the published 1-5 min' for a channel that took an hour. #86 is FIX_CLAIMED and verifications already go to their server on this nodeid. Secondary: `late` is unsorted and the filed reason renders late[0][1] as 'worst {n}s'.

The extractor requires the literal 'MCP ' before the backticked name. Over the three recorded answers it finds three tools in NEX-0002 and ZERO in NEX-0007 and NEX-0008 -- both of which name tools in backticks without the prefix, including find_trade_path and place_order. The docstring says it must catch this on every future answer because the answer is generated per question; it currently sees nothing in two answers out of three.

Asserts the literal '/api/v1/event-cards/positions' appears in the joined prose of scope.counters_do_not_cover. Their captured fix carries the pointer twice -- in the parenthetical AND in the machine-readable event_cards.rows field. Tidying the parenthetical while keeping the block files 'the reader is not told which endpoint carries it' against a body that says exactly that. Same shape as #83 on this same endpoint, which was withdrawn and cost a retraction.

The contract names 'required_flags naming the platform's own paper control'. The assertion only checks the set is NON-EMPTY and never reads what is in it. Renaming agents.clone's required_flags from ['paper'] to ['confirm'] keeps this green, keeps test_a_rule_that_requires_no_flag_is_unaffected green (it pins rule IDs, not flag names) and keeps test_cloning_a_bot_needs_its_paper_flag_too green (it only posts to bots.clone) -- and a MUTATE POST to /api/v1/agents/clone with confirm:true then satisfies the guard with no paper key, which CloneBotRequest resolves against simulation_mode, and that is False.

Docstring says '**Both** clone routes'. /api/v1/agents/clone is never posted to and its rule is never read, so any regression confined to that rule leaves the check green. Together with A05 these two are the only things between a MUTATE test and a live clone on agents/clone, and neither reads that rule's flag.

The docstring says it reads the source rather than the behaviour precisely because 'behaviour can be preserved while the gate is moved somewhere it never runs' -- and the assertion is textual proximity (600 chars after the first 'affordable(' contains 'raise'), which cannot see a move. Relocating the affordable/raise block to just after the POST keeps both tokens in the window: green, and the book refuses an order the platform has already accepted. Cheaper still, a dead helper later in the file containing both tokens satisfies it with no gate in buy() at all. The auditor verified the naive mutation (raise -> print) does go red today.

Contract: 'the refusal has to say what is actually left'. Asserts '5000' in why -- and the message also renders deployed 95000.00, which contains '5000'. True for cash 5000.00, 4999.50, 1.00 and 0.00. A refusal that omits the uncommitted figure entirely still passes.

Every fixture puts `today` AFTER `at`, and the one future-stamp case is +3 weeks, which blesses liveness()'s `0 <= now - stamped` lower bound as correct. An `at` ahead of the clock by HOURS -- clock skew, or a hand-written timestamp -- makes liveness() say 'abandoned' for a pass that is running. Not hypothetical: this pass wrote 21:40Z against a 14:58Z clock and test_no_confirmed_finding_was_left_unfixed_by_a_deep_pass went red mid-pass, which step 6 runs and step 9 reverts a night over. Third instance of this class after the calendar-day comparison and the week read as skipped.

Inherits C01: _pass_in_flight() consults the same liveness(), so on a negative-elapsed stamp it returns None and the staleness assertion runs during the pass after all. Green today only because both NEXT.md items are dated today; a fifteen-day-old open line plus a running pass is a reverted night.

Docstring: 'a schema change here shows up as red.' All three assertions (claimed>=real, voted>=unanimous, header starts with 'pass') are true for ANY input -- each counts a subset of the other, and the header is a constant. The auditor renamed `gaps` and ran it against the real notebooks: every row went to zeros and every assertion still held. An all-zero row exists today and the guard says nothing. versions() also swallows JSONDecodeError and git failure, so unreadable drift ends Inconclusive rather than red.

Asserts keep_set()[id] == 'last-fired', but 'last-fired' is ALSO the reason set by the refusals branch, and admissibility() on that fixture returns four unseen refusal reasons. The auditor deleted the verdict-tracking branch (prune_runs.py:131-134) and the record still came back 'last-fired'. Concrete deletion: a newer record with the same refusals and no measurements plus an older one holding the sole occurrence of a verdict -- the older is a victim, guard green.

cited_run_ids() claims 'every run id anything in the repository still names' and walk() matches only the literal key `run_id`. The fixture only ever spells a citation that way. Real instance: run-20260908T150721Z-435ad0b is named inside a withdraw event's REASON TEXT as the capture proving their fix predated our fail verification -- the evidence for the retraction owed on #83. Structural walk returns 170 ids, a text scan 171. It survives today only as 'young' and becomes a victim in five days.

Asserts no UnicodeEncodeError and rc 0; nothing asserts a body was PRINTED or that it carried a character cp1250 cannot hold. With an empty QA_MEMORY_DIR the auditor got rc 0, empty stdout, 'no memories at ...' -- green having exercised nothing. That is the same machine state tests/repo/test_memories.py explicitly raises Inconclusive for. Written by this pass, tonight.

Asserts the token `printable(` appears somewhere in the file's TEXT. A call moved into a branch that does not run -- or the token in a comment -- keeps it green while `--for` still tracebacks on a cp1250 console. Presence of a token against a contract about what happens before the first print. Written by this pass, tonight.

Only lines beginning exactly with '- [' are held to ITEM, so '* [ ] 2026-09-10 ...' or '-[ ] 2026-09-10 ...' in a hand-edited NEXT.md is an agreed next step to any reader, is never printed by the hook, and is not flagged -- precisely the state the docstring names. Written by this pass, tonight.
